findings.quote: Round-bracket any end the domain leaves out.
findings.problem: This general range shortcut, which the same paragraph applies to parabolas, gives a wrong range when the left-out end's output is also reached at an included input. For y=x^2 on (-2,2], the left-out end x=-2 gives 4, so the shortcut round-brackets 4 and yields [0,4). But x=2 is in the domain and gives 4, so the true range is [0,4]. The same failure occurs for h(x)=(x-2)^2+1 on (0,4]: shortcut gives [1,5), true range [1,5]. The limit (round-bracket only when no included input reaches that output, which always holds for a non-horizontal line but not for a parabola) is not stated. The Core Concept version of the rule is correctly limited to straight lines; the shortcut drops that limit. The definition of range as outputs actually produced partly covers the case, which the lead may weigh.
